target_customer: Canadian (later US) adults facing a planned surgery, sold through brokers and employer benefit plans, with the premium paid per procedure
problem: People going into planned surgery with no life cover, for example after leaving a job with group benefits, have no short term product that pays their family if they die from the procedure.
business_model: Insurance MGA selling one time, per procedure accidental death policies (about CA$90 to CA$150 per policy) underwritten by a partner carrier

founders.name: Eric Blondeel
education: University of Waterloo, BASc chemical engineering (2009)
University of Waterloo, PhD chemical engineering (2018)
founders.background_notes: The idea came from his own 2020 surgery, when he realised he had no life cover after leaving a job with group benefits (University of Waterloo alumni story and BetaKit). Prior employers are not named in the sources.

founders.name: Matt Eggertson
founders.role: Co-founder, built the surgical risk data model
education: University of Waterloo, BASc computer engineering (2010)
founders.background_notes: Described by Waterloo as having a health data analytics background and as having spent time at Y Combinator.

founders.name: Leon Punambolam
founders.role: Co-founder (the only founder listed on the YC page); described as COO or CEO by different directories
founders.background_notes: Insurance executive with about 25 years in the local insurance industry; helped build the underwriting model for surgical risk. Education and employers not named in the sources opened.

technical_complexity.rationale: The hard part was an actuarial and underwriting model for surgical mortality plus a regulated insurance structure with a carrier partner (Berkley Insurance), not software. A small team built the data model; the software itself is standard.

defensibility.rationale: The company called its product the first of its kind in the world for planned surgery in March 2022, and its underwriting model and carrier relationship take time to copy. The idea itself is simple and an established insurer could add a rider.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copy was found in the sources. SiriusPoint, a reinsurer, invested in Samos in 2022 and later press describes a management shake-up at the MGA (paywalled, details unknown).

market_need_then: The founder's own experience of facing surgery without life cover. Samos cited consumer research in its seed announcement that three in five Canadians would buy such a product (newswire headline). Travel insurance was the analogy: a short, statistically predictable risk window.

branding.domain_note: Launched on samos.insure; the root redirects to samos.com, which is now a sparse page reading simple financial security for your loved ones. Date of the move not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain, reassuring insurance language framed as travel insurance for a hospital stay.

branding.brand_signature: Tagline framing as travel insurance for surgery
branding.community_and_virality: Launch coverage in BetaKit, Insurance Business, Insurance Canada and a University of Waterloo alumni story; no sign of community, merch or memes.

brand_strength.rationale: Trade and Canadian tech press covered the launch, but no source shows consumer recognition or brand driven growth. The name is short and neutral.

outcome_analysis: Samos launched in March 2022 as a first of its kind surgical accidental death product, raised a US$3 million seed led by SiriusPoint in July 2022, and remains active per the YC directory. The founder's personal experience gave a clear story and the underwriting model plus carrier backing form a modest moat. A later report mentions a management shake-out at the MGA, so execution risk exists, but no shutdown or exit was found.
notes: Seed round: Insurance Business (28 July 2022) and a Newswire headline both say US$3 million; the CA$3.8 million in the headline is the same round in Canadian dollars. A profile listing total funding of $500K looks wrong. The YC page lists only Leon Punambolam; Blondeel and Eggertson are named as co-founders in the Waterloo story. Directories disagree on whether Punambolam is CEO or COO. No competitor with a source dated near March 2022 was found; the competitor searches returned no named rivals, so the list is empty rather than wrong. Management shake-out headline (Insurance Insider) was paywalled.
